problem:
Consider the bilinear form $B(x,y),$ given by 

$$
B(x,y)=2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-4{x}_{2}{y}_{3}+{x}_{3}{y}_{1}-3{x}_{3}{y}_{2}.
$$

 

Evaluate $B(x,y)$ when $x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

Consider the the bilinear form $B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}),$ given by 

$$
B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})= 2 x_1y_2 - x_2y_2 +3 x_2y_3-x_3y_1
$$

examples.worked_solution:
We are given that 

$\qquad$ ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14043646/assets/652258046237288de7102e402a266dd3afff1abfecf97aa2156a351a7611afb3.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14043646/assets/58ef5fbadaf595035dc902aac9b66bbce61fea79b6a4144ed060f0486dda982c.png) 

Substituting these into the bilinear expression, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{3}-{x}_{3}{y}_{1} \\  & =2\cdot 1\cdot 2-1\cdot 2+3\cdot 1\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot (-2) \\  & =4-2+3-2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
